metadata.scenario_title: DUI Vehicular Manslaughter — State v. Marcus Webb

agents.reason: While the BAC tests are established and the outcome was tragically fatal, the prosecution has not convinced me beyond a reasonable doubt that the statutory culpable mental state and proximate causation have been proved to the required degree. The law requires more than an unfortunate result or an elevated BAC; it requires proof that the defendant's conduct, with the requisite criminal culpability, was the legally attributable cause of the death. Reasonable questions remain about the traffic-signal/timing evidence, witness perceptions, and whether any inference of recklessness or negligence is sufficiently supported by the record. Under the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard, those doubts require acquittal.
